newsitem.title: CHINA: China says no change in diesel ex-refinery price.
newsitem.headline: China says no change in diesel ex-refinery price.

text.p: China's State Planning Commission said on Friday there has been no change in the state-set ex-refinery price for diesel fuel despite market pressure from cheaper illegal imports.
The ex-refinery price remains at 2,190 yuan ($253) per tonne, an official of the commission told Reuters.
Diesel was being quoted at 1,800 yuan per tonne in some parts of the country though this was not an ex-refinery price, he said.
China's eastern and southeastern coastal provinces have reported an influx of smuggled diesel fuel, putting financial pressure on state-owned refiners.
In June, some state refineries in northeastern China said they were allowed to reduce their ex-refinery prices temporarily to help trim high inventories.
The Dalian refinery in Liaoning province said it had been allowed to cut its ex-refinery price to 2,090 yuan.
